task.title: Dirty write-back residency
task.specification: Config slots>=1. Start empty resident cache and durable map, per-key version counters=0. Events write{key,value},read{key},flush{key},ack{key,version},evict{key}. Cache recency is oldest->newest. To insert when full, evict the oldest CLEAN resident; if all dirty insertion fails. Write existing key always succeeds, increments its lifetime version, sets dirty=true and newest; insert write uses same rule, status=written or blocked. Read returns resident value and makes newest (hit); otherwise durable value (durable), must promote it CLEAN if space/clean eviction permits; if every resident is dirty, return the durable value without promotion, without changing lifetime version; absent=miss/null. Flush resident dirty key emits {key,version,value} without changing recency/dirty, status=flushed; otherwise ignored. Ack only for a currently resident dirty entry with version matching both current version AND a previously emitted flush for that key/version: persist current value, mark clean (persisted); otherwise ignored. Evict only clean resident (evicted), dirty=blocked, absent=missing. Other operations value=null. Output {status,value,flush:[records],cached:[oldest-to-newest keys],dirty:[sorted dirty keys],durable:{key:value}}. A stale acknowledgment cannot persist newer unflushed data. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}, initially state=null. Only the current event is supplied; every named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"restore"}. Return exactly the stated output fields each step; opaque JSON state is not graded. All numeric inputs and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; time deltas are nonnegative. Unless a task explicitly overrides this, keys, snapshot IDs, readers and graph nodes are single lowercase ASCII letters. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. At most eight identities and 48 events occur. Configurations and event fields shown below are present. Ordinary regimes use moderate storage and timing; boundary uses equality/empty states; adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events; shift uses smaller capacity, longer timing gaps or deeper dependency shapes, without changing these rules. Generator regimes: Boundary has one resident slot; shift has two versus ordinary three, with write events weighted 3/7 instead of 1/5 to increase dirty pressure; dirty entries cannot be evicted. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Seed banking
matchedCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
matchedCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
matchedCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

sources.title: How to preserve seeds for the future

shuffledCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
shuffledCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
shuffledCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
shuffledCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

initial.explanation: Use a conditional rule tied directly to the first write: a successful first write must make its key the sole newest resident. This rejects the supplied mutations while remaining true for every applicable correct example.
initial.mapping: The resident array is cache recency, entries carry value/version/dirty state, durable stores acknowledged values, and flushSeen records emitted version acknowledgments.
initial.assumptions: Keys are lowercase strings and event fields follow the public contract. Unknown operation types are ignored with value null.
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config||{},e=x.event||{},s=x.state;if(!s)s={r:[],v:{},d:{},f:{}};var r=s.r,v=s.v,d=s.d,f=s.f,k=e.key,i=r.findIndex(function(a){return a.k===k}),a=i<0?null:r[i],status='ignored',value=null,flush=[];function touch(n){var z=r.indexOf(n);if(z>=0)r.splice(z,1);r.push(n)}function cleanSlot(){for(var j=0;j<r.length;j++)if(!r[j].dirty)return j;return -1}function add(n){if(r.length<c.slots){r.push(n);return true}var j=cleanSlot();if(j<0)return false;r.splice(j,1);r.push(n);return true}if(e.type==='write'){if(a){a.value=e.value;a.version=(v[k]||0)+1;v[k]=a.version;a.dirty=true;touch(a);status='written'}else{var n={k:k,value:e.value,version:(v[k]||0)+1,dirty:true};v[k]=n.version;if(add(n))status='written';}}else if(e.type==='read'){if(a){value=a.value;touch(a);status='hit'}else if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(d,k)){value=d[k];var n={k:k,value:value,version:v[k]||0,dirty:false};if(add(n))status='durable';else status='durable'}}else if(e.type==='flush'){if(a&&a.dirty){flush=[{key:k,value:a.value,version:a.version}];f[k]=a.version;status='flushed'}}else if(e.type==='ack'){if(a&&a.dirty&&a.version===e.version&&f[k]===e.version){d[k]=a.value;a.dirty=false;status='persisted'}}else if(e.type==='evict'){if(!a)status='missing';else if(!a.dirty){r.splice(i,1);status='evicted'}else status='blocked'}var dirty=r.filter(function(n){return n.dirty}).map(function(n){return n.k}).sort();var cached=r.map(function(n){return n.k});return{state:s,output:{status:status,value:value,flush:flush,cached:cached,dirty:dirty,durable:d}}}

final.explanation: Maintains recency as an oldest-to-newest array, lifetime versions independently from resident entries, durable values, and the most recently flushed version per key. Writes increment versions even when insertion is blocked. Clean entries may be evicted for insertion or durable promotion; dirty entries cannot. Acknowledgments persist only the currently resident dirty value when its version matches a previously emitted flush.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(!s)s={r:[],v:{},d:{},f:{}};var r=s.r,v=s.v,d=s.d,f=s.f,k=e.key,i=r.findIndex(function(n){return n.k===k}),a=i<0?null:r[i],status='ignored',value=null,flush=[];function touch(n){var j=r.indexOf(n);if(j>=0)r.splice(j,1);r.push(n)}function clean(){for(var j=0;j<r.length;j++)if(!r[j].dirty)return j;return-1}function add(n){if(r.length<c.slots){r.push(n);return true}var j=clean();if(j<0)return false;r.splice(j,1);r.push(n);return true}if(e.type==='write'){var ver=(v[k]||0)+1;v[k]=ver;if(a){a.value=e.value;a.version=ver;a.dirty=true;touch(a);status='written'}else{var n={k:k,value:e.value,version:ver,dirty:true};if(add(n))status='written';else status='blocked'}}else if(e.type==='read'){if(a){value=a.value;touch(a);status='hit'}else if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(d,k)){value=d[k];var n={k:k,value:value,version:v[k]||0,dirty:false};add(n);status='durable'}else status='miss'}else if(e.type==='flush'){if(a&&a.dirty){flush=[{key:k,value:a.value,version:a.version}];f[k]=a.version;status='flushed'}}else if(e.type==='ack'){if(a&&a.dirty&&a.version===e.version&&f[k]===e.version){d[k]=a.value;a.dirty=false;status='persisted'}}else if(e.type==='evict'){if(!a)status='missing';else if(a.dirty)status='blocked';else{r.splice(i,1);status='evicted'}}var dirty=r.filter(function(n){return n.dirty}).map(function(n){return n.k}).sort();return{state:s,output:{status:status,value:value,flush:flush,cached:r.map(function(n){return n.k}),dirty:dirty,durable:d}}}

initial.explanation: Maintain an LRU resident cache, durable map, lifetime versions, and the set of emitted flush versions. Writes dirty entries; acknowledgments persist only the currently flushed version. Reads promote durable values only when a clean slot is available.
initial.mapping: Cache entries map keys to value, version, and dirty state; order is oldest-to-newest. Durable stores acknowledged values. Versions survive eviction, and emitted flush versions authorize matching acknowledgments.
initial.assumptions: Event values are finite JSON values and keys are strings. Unknown event types are treated as no-ops. The supplied slot count is a positive integer.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output))return false;for(const o of output){if(!o||!Array.isArray(o.cached)||!Array.isArray(o.dirty)||!Array.isArray(o.flush)||!o.durable||o.cached.some(k=>typeof k!=="string"||k.includes("__changed")))return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains ordered LRU residency, durable acknowledged values, lifetime versions, and flush authorizations. Insertions evict only the oldest clean entry; blocked writes still advance the key’s lifetime version. Acknowledgments persist only the currently resident dirty version that was previously flushed.

initial.explanation: Maintain an ordered resident cache, durable map, lifetime versions, and per-entry flush eligibility. Writes advance versions; acknowledgments persist only the exact currently flushed version.
initial.mapping: Cache entries map keys to value, version, dirty, and flushed state; order is oldest-to-newest. Durable stores acknowledged values; versions persist independently of residency.
initial.assumptions: Events are valid under the stated contract, keys are strings, and JSON values are safe finite data. Unknown event types are treated as no-ops.

final.explanation: Maintains LRU residency, durable acknowledged values, lifetime versions, and per-entry flush eligibility. Writes always advance the key version; blocked insertions retain that counter. Acknowledgment persists only a dirty resident whose version matches a previously flushed version, preventing stale acknowledgments from persisting newer data.
